completed_stage_receipts.summary: Confirmed a control-plane state-drift defect: the user explicitly reports deleting the Continuity monitors and current product-state reread shows the declared core monitor tasks absent, while durable/rebuildable repository surfaces still claim them enabled or hourly-active. The user deletion is intentional product mutation; the defect is stale repository liveness representation, not the deletion itself.

Classified the failure as external-product-observation-staleness: mutable ChatGPT automation state can change outside repository writes, so a past enabled observation cannot remain represented as current liveness truth. User intent to delete must not be auto-reversed.

Mapped the affected path: live ChatGPT automation product state -> monitor liveness observation -> rebuildable HARNESS_STATUS -> authoritative maintenance manifest/handoff summary -> future maintenance decisions. Bypass surface is any external product mutation that does not also write GitHub. BUSINESS owner state and leases are out of scope.

Prior mitigation used peer liveness checks but explicitly could not detect simultaneous loss of all monitors. This new user-initiated all-monitor deletion is a known-class recurrence at the product/repository boundary. Escalation therefore moves above peer-watch repair to the state-authority model: repository may retain expectation/last-observed evidence, but current product liveness must require fresh product re-observation and must never be inferred from a stale durable flag.
